transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. The minute I even get near blood tests or needles, I feel an immediate wave of fear that makes me want to bolt from the clinic. It's pretty embarrassing to admit, but it has gotten to the point where I just can't ignore it anymore.
When you’re around needles or blood tests, do you ever feel faint, dizzy, or actually pass out? Or is it mainly intense fear without those physical reactions?

I definitely get both—it's a massive wave of fear along with some really intense physical reactions. My chest tightens, my heart starts pounding, my hands get sweaty, and I feel like I might pass out the entire time I'm forced to sit through it.

When you’re exposed to needles or blood, do you first feel your heart race and then suddenly feel lightheaded or faint, or is it mainly panic the whole time without that sudden drop? Have you ever actually fainted during a blood draw or injection?

My heart races and my chest tightens with intense panic right away, but I also feel extremely lightheaded and feel like I might pass out the entire time. I've never actually fully fainted, but I have to white-knuckle it and grip the chair just to get through it.

Is your fear limited to needles and blood tests, or do you react the same way to other things like seeing blood, injuries, or medical procedures? Do you actively avoid those situations because of this fear?

My fear is highly focused on needles, shots, blood draws, and IVs, but it has made me dread and avoid medical settings and procedures in general. I actively avoid these situations by rescheduling my own appointments, making excuses, and dropping my sister off at the curb instead of going inside with her. If I absolutely have to stay, I end up white-knuckling it and feeling like I might pass out the entire time.

Besides needles and blood draws, do you get the same intense fear or faint feeling when you see blood, injuries, or medical procedures on TV or in real life? Or is it only when something might be done to your own body?

It is definitely not just when it's done to my own body, as watching my sister get her IV infusion is actually what triggered this severe fear in the first place. Now, even seeing needles or medical tubes on other people, or even watching medical procedures on TV, makes me incredibly anxious and uncomfortable. That is exactly why I have to drop my sister off at the curb instead of going inside with her.
